propositions: Five distinct sites classify git failure strings with inconsistent verdicts for identical text, causing `cannot lock ref` to receive three different outcomes depending on operation context.

The synthetic rc-124 `git timed out after` result is constructed at four sites with no unified retry policy, leaving `sync._union_merge` and `push_recovery` without transient retry despite needing it.

A single `classify(result, *, operation) -> GitOutcome` function with operation-keyed registry (local, commit, push, lease-push, ref-cas) must disambiguate markers and structural predicates like `_is_cas_mismatch` that depend on command shape and exit code.

`cannot lock ref` must preserve three deliberately different verdicts: retriable local lock under `local` operation, non-lease push reject under `lease-push` operation (excluding `--force-with-lease` mismatches per bugs 4afc and ebee), and held advisory lock terminal under `ref-cas` operation.

The tenth outcome kind `INVALID_OBJECT` (git write-tree refusing missing objects) must remain distinct from `FATAL` to preserve its index-rebuild-then-retry recovery action rather than terminal failure.

Two guards enforce consolidation: Guard A prevents marker strings appearing as code literals outside `git_outcome.py` (owner-exempt module); Guard B prevents synthetic-timeout construction outside `gitutil.py` within `src/rebar/_store` scope, permitting only one `run_git_bounded` definition.
